short: Cu clusters immobilized on Cd-defective cadmium sulfide nano
title: Cu clusters immobilized on Cd-defective cadmium sulfide nano-rods towards photocatalytic CO2 reduction

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Metal clusters normally need protecting ligands, which then block the sites that would do the chemistry. Cation vacancies at a sulfide edge should trap bare metal clusters and hold them there without ligands.
states.detail: Absorbed: n2 (HYP/gap), n3 (HYP/hypothesis), n4 (DES/base_system), n5 (DES/modification), n6 (DES/route), n7 (DES/variable_sweep), n8 (PRC/synthesis), n9 (PRC/treatment), n10 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Rods 100-300 nm long, sharpened at the edges after treatment. Cd vacancies line the edges of the nanorods.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (STR/microstructure/shape), n12 (STR/defect/point), n13 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n14 (STR/interface). Premises: Cu K-edge shoulders at 8980.9, 8982.1 and 8986.4 eV mark metallic Cu, Cu(1+) and Cu(2+); Cu-S bonding is reported to put the wavelet intensity maximum near 4.9 inverse angstrom

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The Cu-S interface pulls electron density off the sulfide, and the resulting internal field drives photoelectrons onto the clusters. Cd and S core levels shift up in binding energy and the carrier lifetime lengthens from 1.00 to 1.14 ns.
states.detail: Absorbed: n15 (MEC/pathway), n16 (PRP/descriptor), n17 (PRP/value), n18 (MEC/identification). Premises: Spin-polarised DFT on a 38-atom Cu cluster at a vacancy on the defective CdS (100) surface

states.title: Performance state
states.head: CO yield of 38.3 umol/g in 5 h, an average 7.7 umol/g/h, with no sacrificial agent. Turnover number 94.4 at 81.1% CO selectivity, against 54.4 at 72.2% for the bare rods

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Cd vacancies immobilise ligand-free Cu clusters that both bind and activate CO2 and drain the photoelectrons

nodes.title: PL:timeresolved, XPS, F5
nodes.head: Cd 3d and S 2p both move about 0.8 eV to higher binding energy when the Cu clusters are present. Single-exponential PL lifetimes are 1.14, 1.07 and 1.00 ns for CuCR SCC, CR-H and CR
nodes.solves: Cd and S core levels shift up in binding energy and the carrier lifetime lengthens from 1.00 to 1.14 ns
nodes.note: shifts read between the dotted guide lines in F5a and F5b; the CuCR SCC S 2p envelope is also noticeably broader lifetimes and chi-squared are printed on F5d, F5e and F5f; the three decay curves look alike by eye and the fits start only at 5 ns, so a 14% spread is near what the data can carry

nodes.title: DERIVED, F5
nodes.head: Isosteric heat starts at 25.4 kJ/mol for CuCR SCC against 8.9 for CR, then falls below it beyond ~0.075 mmol/g
nodes.solves: CO2 binds far more strongly at low coverage: isosteric heat 25.4 against 8.9 kJ/mol
nodes.note: read from F5h. CuCR SCC starts at ~25.4 kJ/mol at the lowest uptake against ~8.9 for CR, the two cross near 0.072 mmol/g, CuCR SCC bottoms out near 3.0 kJ/mol at 0.105 mmol/g and then climbs back through the CR curve at about 0.125, reaching ~11.5 at 0.145. CR falls only from 8.9 to a shallow minimum of ~4.3 and back to ~4.6. So the Cu catalyst is the weaker binder only over a middle window, not at every uptake above the crossing.
nodes.detail: o9: Isosteric heat starts at 25.4 kJ/mol for CuCR SCC against 8.9 for CR, then falls below it beyond ~0.075 mmol/g
